clue.text: British crossword setter keeping green suit

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the setter's letters hold the green word

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as ME
eco- means environmentally friendly, i.e. green

explanation.surface: A British setter keeps a green suit in the wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like the item of clothing the setter keeps, but it is a verb: that colour suits you.
explanation.definitionFit: To become someone is to look good on them, as a colour or outfit flatters its wearer.

clue.text: Keen on men and women, faction split in half

parts.note: bi is short for bisexual
a sect is a breakaway group or faction

explanation.surface: A faction keen on both sexes splits in half.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts, a geometry term for halving.

clue.text: Unfinished Indian dish — starters of it coming up later among courses

indicators.note: unfinished means the dish loses its final letter

parts.note: a curry is a spiced Indian dish

indicators.note: starters of means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A meal description: a curry left half-eaten, with more starters arriving later among the courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' looks like part of the meal, but it is the definition, in its educational sense. 'coming up later among' is not a direction: those words just supply their initials ICULA.
explanation.definitionFit: Curricula are the plural of curriculum, the programmes of study offered as school or college courses.

clue.text: Game briefly cooked with herb in African region

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients being reworked into a new arrangement
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before shortening

explanation.surface: Game cooked with a herb sounds like a North African recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maghreb is the region of north-west Africa covering Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

clue.text: Criminal more self-satisfied when pocketing pound

indicators.note: pocketing means putting something inside, as into a pocket

parts.note: smugger is the comparative of smug
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A villain grows smugger as he pockets the money.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler is a lawbreaker who moves contraband goods illegally across borders.

clue.text: Curse the way men enunciate

definitions.meaning: second, punning meaning: ..., diction being the way one enunciates

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into MALE and DICTION, diction being the way someone pronounces words.
explanation.definitionFit: A malediction is a spoken curse, the opposite of a benediction.

clue.text: Cultured chap, a slippery customer

parts.note: a gent is a man or chap
an eel is proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: A refined man who turns out to be a slippery character.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means polite and refined in manner, as a cultured person is.

clue.text: Tool used to shape large articles

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A workshop tool for shaping big objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like objects being shaped, but it means the grammatical words A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins a workpiece so a cutting tool can shape it, typically wood or metal.

clue.text: Model desiring great place to sit

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A model wants a prime seat at a fashion show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside seats beside a boxing ring or arena are prized for their close view.

clue.text: Sort of rock eaten by two lots of small children

indicators.note: eaten by means held inside the other letters

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, taken twice
prog rock is progressive rock music

explanation.surface: Small children munching a type of rock, perhaps a seaside stick of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprogs is British slang for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is informal British slang for a child or baby.

clue.text: Small sea organisms in large quantity on board

indicators.note: on means one piece follows on after the other

parts.note: a plank is a board of wood
a ton, as in tons of something, is a large quantity

explanation.surface: Huge numbers of tiny sea creatures washed up on a deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are the minute drifting plants and animals floating in the sea.

clue.text: Awfully rich Republican and leading editor tweeted

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: up means ahead or leading, as in a goal up

explanation.surface: A wealthy Republican and a top editor posted on Twitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweeted' suggests posting online, but here it is birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: To chirrup is to make the short high chirping sounds of a small bird.

clue.text: Least tanned, trendy Scot one encountered in the Middle East

definitions.text: one encountered in the Middle East

parts.note: palest is the superlative of pale
in means fashionable
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A pale fashionable Scot meets someone on a Middle East trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A Palestinian is a person from Palestine, a region in the Middle East.

clue.text: What odds might be — or what they certainly aren't!

definitions.meaning: betting odds of one to one are called ...
odd numbers are by definition not even

explanation.walkthrough: The same word 'odds' is read first as a bookmaker's price, then as odd numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is the bookmaker's price for an even-money bet, and even numbers are the opposite of odd ones.

clue.text: Rocking crib with loud claim this connects mother and child

indicators.note: rocking suggests shaking the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A nursery scene: a rocking crib and a noisy demand from the baby.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbilical cord links a foetus to the placenta, joining it to the mother before birth.

clue.text: Oscar determined to bag M & S products that soothe

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to bag is to capture or enclose, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: intent means resolved or determined

explanation.surface: Someone called Oscar is set on buying soothing products at Marks & Spencer.
explanation.walkthrough: M & S is Marks & Spencer, a British high-street store; here its letters are used separately, M inside the word for determined and S added after.
explanation.definitionFit: Ointments are greasy preparations rubbed on the skin to heal or soothe.

clue.text: About to leave very moreish food enhancer

indicators.note: to leave means a letter departs from the word

parts.note: addictive food is so moreish you cannot stop eating
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A flavour enhancer that makes food irresistibly moreish.
explanation.walkthrough: Moreish is British slang for food so tasty you want more.
explanation.definitionFit: An additive is a substance added to food to improve flavour, colour or shelf life.

clue.text: Doctor identifying ailments indicating a case of otitis needs treating

indicators.note: treating suggests working on the letters to rearrange them
a case is the outside, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A doctor deciding that an ear infection needs treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is not the anagram signal here; it opens the definition. Otitis is an ear infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagnostician is a medical specialist skilled in working out the cause of illness.

clue.text: Remarkably majestically welcoming cheers

indicators.note: welcoming means letting another in, so letters go inside

parts.note: nobly means in a grand, majestic manner
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A grand and stately welcome with cheering.
explanation.definitionFit: Notably means in a striking way that deserves notice, especially so.

clue.text: Encroachments where the Colossus stood, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the phrase

parts.note: the Colossus of Rhodes stood in Rhodes

explanation.surface: Historical trivia about the site of an ancient statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are advances made into territory or a market at another's expense.

clue.text: Like old Tory PM Robert, turning up in a comatose state

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century Conservative Prime Minister

explanation.surface: An old Tory PM found unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Asleep describes being unconscious in slumber, a comatose condition.

clue.text: Captain lethargically tours strip of water

indicators.note: tours means going around, so the letters are held across the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sleepy captain sailing around a narrow waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of sea or lake reaching into the land.

clue.text: Hillsides not primarily suitable for runs

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: slopes are hillsides

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Hillsides that are no good for skiing runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like ski runs on the slopes, but it is a verb: to lope is to run with long strides.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to move with long easy bounding strides, a relaxed way of running.

clue.text: Person knowing little criminal roaming America

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are badly treated and rearranged

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A foolish lawbreaker wandering across America.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant or uneducated person.

clue.text: Where drinkers are left in charge openly

parts.note: drinkers are found in a pub

explanation.surface: Drinkers in a pub are left in charge without concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: In public means openly, where others can see, not in private.

clue.text: Son getting Schwarzenegger lunch, perhaps

parts.note: Arnie is the nickname of actor Arnold Schwarzenegger

explanation.surface: A son eats lunch with Schwarzenegger.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarnie is British slang for a sandwich; 'perhaps' shows lunch is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarnie, an informal sandwich, is a typical midday meal eaten on the go.

clue.text: Trying extremely efficacious maxim

indicators.note: extremely means the very ends of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: a saying is a maxim or proverb

explanation.surface: Attempting a highly effective motto.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it, so essaying means making an attempt.

clue.text: Consumes a portion of grouse supper

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone eats part of a game-bird dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up something is to exhaust or eat all of it, a phrasal verb for consuming.
